<!-- Generated by tools/docgen from doc comments. Do not edit: run scripts/docs.sh. -->

```odin
import testkit "fire:testkit"
```

Test-only toolkit for nodes: signal generators, analyzers, WAV I/O, golden
files, the null backend (`render`), a probe node, and real-device loopback
helpers.

A typical test builds an input with the generators, renders the node through
the null backend (which traps allocations inside `process`, fills outputs with
NaN so unwritten samples show up, and varies the block size), checks the report
with `expect_clean_render`, then asserts behavior with the analyzers:

```odin
n := dsp.gain_create()
defer core.node_destroy(&n)

input := testkit.buffer_make(2, 48_000, 48_000, context.temp_allocator)
testkit.sine(input.channels[0], 48_000, 440, 0.5)
testkit.buffer_mono_to_all(input)

cfg := testkit.default_render_config()
cfg.blocks = testkit.Random_Blocks{seed = 1, min = 0, max = cfg.max_block}
out, report := testkit.render(&n, input, cfg, context.temp_allocator)
defer testkit.render_report_destroy(&report)
testkit.expect_clean_render(t, report)
testkit.expect_near(t, testkit.tone_amplitude(out.channels[0], 48_000, 440), 0.5, 1e-3, "level")
```

Add `expect_block_invariant` with `standard_block_patterns` for any node that
takes events, and `expect_golden` to pin down exact output.

Engine packages must never import testkit.

## Constants

### RENDER_TIMELINE

```odin
RENDER_TIMELINE : core.Timeline_Id : core.Timeline_Id{0, 1}
```

The one timeline in `render`'s transport snapshot. It leads, and when
`Render_Config.playing` is set its position equals the grid.

## Types

### Compare_Result

```odin
Compare_Result :: struct {
	max_abs_error: f64,
	max_error_at: int,
	max_error_ch: int,
	rms_error: f64,
	error_db: f64,
	frame_mismatch: bool,
}
```

Outcome of `compare_slices` / `compare_buffers`. Errors are absolute (linear)
sample differences, `actual - expected`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `max_abs_error` | largest \|actual - expected\| |
| `max_error_at` | frame index of max_abs_error |
| `max_error_ch` | channel of max_abs_error (compare_buffers only) |
| `rms_error` | RMS of the difference |
| `error_db` | rms_error relative to the reference RMS, in dB |
| `frame_mismatch` | lengths or channel counts differ; only the overlap was compared |

### Audio_Buffer

```odin
Audio_Buffer :: struct {
	channels: [][]f32,
	frames: int,
	sample_rate: f64,
	storage: []f32,
	allocator: mem.Allocator,
}
```

Planar multichannel buffer that owns its storage.

### Loop_Recorder

```odin
Loop_Recorder :: struct {
	play: []f32,
	rec: [2][]f32,
	next_time: i64,
	gaps: int,
	blocks: u64,
	xrun_blocks: int,
	max_entry_skew: i64,
	time_order_bad: int,
	non_monotonic: int,
	last_output_ns: u64,
	stall_ns: i64,
}
```

A Device_Callback for real-device tests: plays `play` (mono, on every
output) and records every input, both indexed by sample_time, and checks the
block contract and timestamps as it goes.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `play` | mono signal played on every output, indexed by sample_time |
| `rec` | first two inputs, indexed by sample_time |
| `next_time` | atomic |
| `gaps` | sample_time discontinuities |
| `blocks` | atomic: callbacks so far |
| `xrun_blocks` | blocks with the xrun flag set |
| `max_entry_skew` | \|host_time_ns() at entry − callback_ns\| |
| `time_order_bad` | blocks where input_ns ≤ callback_ns ≤ output_ns fails (known times only) |
| `non_monotonic` | output_ns did not increase |
| `last_output_ns` |  |
| `stall_ns` | atomic: sleep this long once, in the next block (forces an xrun) |

### Loopback_Result

```odin
Loopback_Result :: struct {
	latency: int,
	gain: f64,
	residual: f64,
	at: int,
	found: bool,
}
```

Outcome of `analyze_loopback`. Only meaningful when `found` is true.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `latency` | frames from play to rec |
| `gain` | least-squares rec / play |
| `residual` | max \|rec − gain·play\| after alignment |
| `at` | where the residual peaks |
| `found` | false if no positive latency within max_lag, or `play` is silent |

### Device_Lock

```odin
Device_Lock :: struct {
	fd: posix.FD,
}
```

Real-device tests share physical devices, so they take turns: a mutex
within the process, and a lock file across processes (test.sh runs each
package once per optimization level, concurrently). POSIX record locks
belong to the process, hence both. The OS drops the file lock on a crash.

### Node_Factory

```odin
Node_Factory :: struct {
	create: proc(user: rawptr) -> core.Node,
	user: rawptr,
}
```

Creates a fresh node for each render in `expect_block_invariant`. `create` is
called with `user`; the caller of the check destroys each node it returns.

### Window

```odin
Window :: enum int {
	Rectangular,
	Hann,
	Blackman_Harris,
}
```

Analysis window for `spectrum` and `window_value`.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `Rectangular` | no window |
| `Hann` | good general choice, ~-31 dB sidelobes |
| `Blackman_Harris` | 4-term, ~-92 dB sidelobes |

### Spectrum

```odin
Spectrum :: struct {
	magnitude: []f64,
	n_fft: int,
	sample_rate: f64,
}
```

Single-sided amplitude spectrum, scaled so a full-scale sine reads ~1.0 at its bin.
The signal is zero-padded to a power of two. Bin k is at k * sample_rate / n_fft.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `magnitude` | n_fft/2 + 1 bins, linear amplitude |
| `n_fft` | FFT length (power of two) |
| `sample_rate` | Hz |

### Rng

```odin
Rng :: struct {
	state: u64,
}
```

Seedable PRNG (SplitMix64). Same seed => same signal on every platform.

### Fixed_Blocks

```odin
Fixed_Blocks :: struct {
	size: int,
}
```

Every block is `size` frames (must be > 0); the last one may be shorter.

### Block_Sequence

```odin
Block_Sequence :: struct {
	sizes: [16]int,
	count: int,
}
```

Cycles through `sizes[:count]`. Build with `block_sequence(...)`.

### Random_Blocks

```odin
Random_Blocks :: struct {
	seed: u64,
	min: int,
	max: int,
}
```

Uniformly random sizes in [min, max] (0 allowed), reproducible from `seed`.

### Block_Pattern

```odin
Block_Pattern :: union {
	Fixed_Blocks,
	Block_Sequence,
	Random_Blocks,
}
```

How `render` splits the signal into `process` calls. Every size is clamped to
[0, max_block] and to the frames remaining.

### Timed_Event

```odin
Timed_Event :: struct {
	time: timebase.Sample_Time,
	payload: core.Event_Payload,
}
```

An event at an absolute frame position from the start of the render.

### Block_Hook

```odin
Block_Hook :: proc(user: rawptr, block_index: int, ctx: ^core.Process_Context)
```

Called by `render` after each process call with the context that was just
processed. Runs outside the trap allocator, so it may allocate.

### Render_Config

```odin
Render_Config :: struct {
	sample_rate: f64,
	max_block: int,
	out_channels: int,
	blocks: Block_Pattern,
	events: []Timed_Event,
	tail_frames: int,
	tempo_bpm: f64,
	tempo_map: ^timebase.Tempo_Map,
	playing: bool,
	ftz: bool,
	max_events_out: int,
	after_block: Block_Hook,
	user: rawptr,
}
```

Settings for one `render`. Start from `default_render_config` and override fields.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `sample_rate` | Hz |
| `max_block` | largest block passed to process, and the prepare max_block |
| `out_channels` | output channel count (input count comes from the input buffer) |
| `blocks` | nil => Fixed_Blocks{max_block} |
| `events` | any order; stable-sorted by time |
| `tail_frames` | extra frames rendered after the input ends (silent input) |
| `tempo_bpm` | constant tempo for the transport |
| `tempo_map` | overrides tempo_bpm when set |
| `playing` | RENDER_TIMELINE is playing (it leads, and follows the grid from beat 0) |
| `ftz` | enable flush-to-zero during process, as on a real audio thread |
| `max_events_out` | output event capacity per block; extra events count as dropped |
| `after_block` | Called after each process call, outside the trap (it may allocate). |
| `user` | passed to after_block |

### Timing_Stats

```odin
Timing_Stats :: struct {
	p50_ns: i64,
	p99_ns: i64,
	max_ns: i64,
	max_load: f64,
	total_ns: i64,
}
```

Wall-clock time of the node's `process` calls over a render. Indicative only: the
null backend runs offline, so treat it as a rough budget check.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `p50_ns` |  |
| `p99_ns` |  |
| `max_ns` | per-call process time percentiles, nanoseconds |
| `max_load` | Worst ratio of process time to the block's real-time duration (1.0 = deadline). |
| `total_ns` | sum of all process calls, nanoseconds |

### Render_Report

```odin
Render_Report :: struct {
	prepare_error: core.Error,
	blocks: int,
	frames: int,
	min_block_used: int,
	max_block_used: int,
	rt_allocations: int,
	first_rt_alloc: runtime.Source_Code_Location,
	non_finite: int,
	first_non_finite: int,
	denormals: int,
	events_out: [dynamic]Timed_Event,
	events_dropped: int,
	timing: Timing_Stats,
}
```

What `render` observed. Pass it to `expect_clean_render`, then free it with
`render_report_destroy`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `prepare_error` | non-.None means prepare failed and nothing was rendered |
| `blocks` | process calls made (including 0-frame ones) |
| `frames` | total frames rendered (input frames + tail_frames) |
| `min_block_used` |  |
| `max_block_used` |  |
| `rt_allocations` | allocation attempts inside process (all were refused) |
| `first_rt_alloc` | call site of the first one |
| `non_finite` | NaN/Inf in output (includes samples the node never wrote) |
| `first_non_finite` | frame index, -1 if none |
| `denormals` | subnormal output samples |
| `events_out` | events the node wrote, at absolute frames; from render's allocator |
| `events_dropped` | events lost to a full output buffer (see max_events_out) |
| `timing` |  |

### Probe_Event

```odin
Probe_Event :: struct {
	block: int,
	offset: u32,
	absolute: timebase.Sample_Time,
	payload: core.Event_Payload,
}
```

One event as the probe received it.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `block` | index of the process call |
| `offset` | frame offset within the block |
| `absolute` | transport.frame + offset |
| `payload` |  |

### Probe_Block

```odin
Probe_Block :: struct {
	frames: int,
	transport: core.Transport,
}
```

One process call as the probe saw it.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `frames` | frames in this call |
| `transport` | copy of the transport at this call, with `timelines` set to nil (it would dangle) |

### Probe

```odin
Probe :: struct {
	log_allocator: mem.Allocator,
	events: []Probe_Event,
	event_count: int,
	blocks: []Probe_Block,
	block_count: int,
	overflow: int,
	unsorted_events: int,
	out_of_range: int,
	capacity: int,
}
```

State of a probe node. Read the log with `probe_events` and `probe_blocks`; it
stays valid after `render` releases the node, until the node is destroyed.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `log_allocator` | the log lives until destroy, so it can be read after release |
| `events` | log storage; use probe_events |
| `event_count` |  |
| `blocks` | log storage; use probe_blocks |
| `block_count` |  |
| `overflow` | events or blocks not recorded because the log was full |
| `unsorted_events` | events whose offset < previous offset in the same block |
| `out_of_range` | events whose offset >= frames |
| `capacity` | log size, set by probe_create |

### Stretch_Signal

```odin
Stretch_Signal :: enum i32 {
	Sweep,
	Drums,
	Voice,
}
```

The test signals for time-stretch reference cases.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `Sweep` | a log sine sweep, 50 Hz to 12 kHz, at −6 dBFS |
| `Drums` | synthetic kick, snare and hi-hats at 120 BPM |
| `Voice` | a gliding pulse train through three formant resonators (an "ah") |

### Stretch_Mode

```odin
Stretch_Mode :: enum i32 {
	Stream,
	Stream_Flush,
	Stream_Seek,
	Exact,
}
```

How a reference case drives the stretcher.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `Stream` | output_seek at the start, then process in chunks |
| `Stream_Flush` | as Stream, then flush the last `flush_frames` |
| `Stream_Seek` | as Stream, seeking to `seek_to_in` once `seek_at_out` frames are out |
| `Exact` | the whole input to the whole output in one exact() call |

### Stretch_Case

```odin
Stretch_Case :: struct {
	name: cstring,
	signal: Stretch_Signal,
	sample_rate: f32,
	channels: i32,
	in_frames: i32,
	out_frames: i32,
	cheaper: b32,
	split: b32,
	rate: f32,
	transpose: f32,
	tonality_limit: f32,
	formant: f32,
	formant_compensate: b32,
	formant_base: f32,
	freq_map: i32,
	mode: Stretch_Mode,
	flush_frames: i32,
	seek_at_out: i32,
	seek_to_in: i32,
	chunks: [4]i32,
	tolerance: f32,
}
```

One reference case for the time-stretcher: its input, settings and how
it is driven. The C++ Signalsmith Stretch rendered these into the
recordings in tests/golden/stretch (before it was removed: see commit
33600b9); the pure-Odin port renders the same cases and is compared with
them.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `name` |  |
| `signal` |  |
| `sample_rate` |  |
| `channels` |  |
| `in_frames` |  |
| `out_frames` | total output, including any flush |
| `cheaper` | presetCheaper instead of presetDefault |
| `split` | split computation |
| `rate` | input frames per output frame |
| `transpose` | frequency factor; 1 = none |
| `tonality_limit` | as a fraction of the sample rate; 0 = none |
| `formant` | formant factor; 1 = none |
| `formant_compensate` |  |
| `formant_base` | Hz; 0 = detect |
| `freq_map` | 0 = none, 1 = `stretch_case_freq_map` |
| `mode` |  |
| `flush_frames` |  |
| `seek_at_out` |  |
| `seek_to_in` |  |
| `chunks` | output frames per process call, repeated; zero entries end the list |
| `tolerance` | The largest spectral distance (`spectral_distance`, dB) allowed from the recording: 1.5 × the C++'s own largest distance on Linux, on Windows, or with its input nudged by −100 dBFS, and at least 0.05 dB (tests/golden/stretch/README.md). |

### Trap_Allocator

```odin
Trap_Allocator :: struct {
	violations: int,
	first_loc: runtime.Source_Code_Location,
	first_mode: runtime.Allocator_Mode,
}
```

An allocator that refuses every request and records it. Installed as both
context.allocator and context.temp_allocator around each `process` call, so any
allocation on the audio thread fails the test, along with its call site.

### Wav_Error

```odin
Wav_Error :: enum int {
	None,
	Io,
	Not_Riff_Wave,
	Missing_Chunk,
	Unsupported_Format,
}
```

Result of `wav_read` and `wav_write`.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `None` |  |
| `Io` | file could not be read or written |
| `Not_Riff_Wave` | not a RIFF/WAVE file |
| `Missing_Chunk` | no fmt or data chunk |
| `Unsupported_Format` | sample format other than those wav_read lists |

## Procedures

### linear_to_db

```odin
linear_to_db :: proc(x: f64) -> f64
```

Converts a linear amplitude to dB (20·log10|x|). Zero maps to about -600 dB instead of -Inf.

### db_to_linear

```odin
db_to_linear :: proc(db: f64) -> f64
```

Converts dB to a linear amplitude factor (10^(db/20)).

### peak

```odin
peak :: proc(x: []f32) -> f64
```

Largest absolute sample value (linear). 0 for an empty slice.

### rms

```odin
rms :: proc(x: []f32) -> f64
```

Root-mean-square level (linear). 0 for an empty slice.

### dc_offset

```odin
dc_offset :: proc(x: []f32) -> f64
```

Mean sample value (linear). 0 for an empty slice.

### count_non_finite

```odin
count_non_finite :: proc(x: []f32) -> (count: int, first_index: int)
```

Counts NaN and Inf samples. `first_index` is the index of the first one, or -1 if none.

### count_denormals

```odin
count_denormals :: proc(x: []f32) -> int
```

Counts subnormal (denormal) f32 samples. Denormals are slow on most CPUs and
usually mean a decaying state variable was not flushed to zero.

### max_step

```odin
max_step :: proc(x: []f32) -> (value: f64, index: int)
```

Largest |x[n] - x[n-1]|. A hard parameter jump or a discontinuity shows up here.

### max_curvature

```odin
max_curvature :: proc(x: []f32) -> (value: f64, index: int)
```

Largest |x[n] - 2x[n-1] + x[n-2]|. A smooth signal of frequency f and amplitude A
stays under A*(2π f/fs)^2; clicks and zipper noise spike far above that.

### sine_curvature_bound

```odin
sine_curvature_bound :: proc(amplitude: f64, freq_hz: f64, sample_rate: f64) -> f64
```

Bound on max_curvature for a clean sine; use as a click threshold with a margin.

### tone_amplitude

```odin
tone_amplitude :: proc(x: []f32, sample_rate: f64, freq_hz: f64) -> f64
```

Amplitude of the component at `freq_hz` using a Hann-windowed single-bin DFT.
A sine of amplitude A reads ~A when the signal spans many cycles.

### response_at

```odin
response_at :: proc(ir: []f32, sample_rate: f64, freq_hz: f64) -> complex128
```

Complex DFT of a (fully decayed) impulse response at one frequency.

### response_db

```odin
response_db :: proc(ir: []f32, sample_rate: f64, freq_hz: f64) -> f64
```

Magnitude response in dB of an impulse response at `freq_hz`.

### response_phase

```odin
response_phase :: proc(ir: []f32, sample_rate: f64, freq_hz: f64) -> f64
```

Phase response in radians of an impulse response at `freq_hz`.

### thd_n_db

```odin
thd_n_db :: proc(x: []f32, sample_rate: f64, fundamental_hz: f64) -> f64
```

THD+N in dB: residual after a least-squares fit of DC + sine at `fundamental_hz`,
relative to the fitted sine's RMS. A clean sine gives a very negative number.

### estimate_latency

```odin
estimate_latency :: proc(reference: []f32, output: []f32, max_lag: int) -> int
```

Delay of `output` relative to `reference`, in frames, by brute-force cross-correlation
over lags 0..max_lag. Returns the lag with the largest |correlation|.

### compare_slices

```odin
compare_slices :: proc(expected: []f32, actual: []f32) -> Compare_Result
```

Compares two mono signals sample by sample over their common length. Sets
`frame_mismatch` if the lengths differ. A NaN difference counts as the worst error.

### compare_buffers

```odin
compare_buffers :: proc(expected: Audio_Buffer, actual: Audio_Buffer) -> Compare_Result
```

Compares two multichannel buffers channel by channel and returns the result of the
channel with the largest `max_abs_error` (`max_error_ch` says which). Sets
`frame_mismatch` if channel counts or frame counts differ.

### spectral_distance

```odin
spectral_distance :: proc(a: []f32, b: []f32, sample_rate: f64, frame: int = 2048) -> f64
```

How different two signals sound, ignoring phase: the mean over
`frame`-sample frames (Hann-windowed, hopping by `frame`) of the RMS
difference in dB between their magnitude spectra, over bins where either
is above −100 dBFS. 0 for identical spectra. Use it where waveforms may
legitimately diverge (a phase vocoder amplifies the last bit of rounding)
but the sound must not. Compares the common length of `a` and `b`.

### buffer_make

```odin
buffer_make :: proc(channels: int, frames: int, sample_rate: f64, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> Audio_Buffer
```

Allocates a zeroed buffer of `channels` x `frames` from `allocator` (one contiguous
block plus the channel slice table). Free with `buffer_destroy`, or let a temp
allocator reclaim it.

### buffer_destroy

```odin
buffer_destroy :: proc(b: ^Audio_Buffer)
```

Frees a buffer made by `buffer_make`, `buffer_clone` or `wav_read` with the allocator
it was made with, and zeroes it.

### buffer_clone

```odin
buffer_clone :: proc(src: Audio_Buffer, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> Audio_Buffer
```

Deep copy of `src` (same channels, frames and sample rate), allocated from `allocator`.

### buffer_mono_to_all

```odin
buffer_mono_to_all :: proc(b: Audio_Buffer)
```

Same signal in every channel: generate into channel 0, then copy.

### buffer_length_only

```odin
buffer_length_only :: proc(frames: int, sample_rate: f64) -> Audio_Buffer
```

A zero-channel buffer that only says how many frames to render (for generators).

### seconds_to_frames

```odin
seconds_to_frames :: proc(seconds: f64, sample_rate: f64) -> int
```

Converts a duration in seconds to frames at `sample_rate`, rounded to the nearest frame.

### loop_recorder_make

```odin
loop_recorder_make :: proc(frames: int, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> ^Loop_Recorder
```

Allocates a recorder (and its `play` and two `rec` channels of `frames` frames each)
from `allocator`. Fill `play` before starting the device. Free with
`loop_recorder_destroy` using the same allocator.

### loop_recorder_destroy

```odin
loop_recorder_destroy :: proc(r: ^Loop_Recorder, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator)
```

Frees a recorder made by `loop_recorder_make`. Pass the allocator it was made with.

### loop_recorder_callback

```odin
loop_recorder_callback :: proc(r: ^Loop_Recorder) -> backend.Device_Callback
```

The `backend.Device_Callback` to hand to the device; it runs `loop_recorder_process`
with `r` as its user pointer. `r` must outlive the stream.

### loop_recorder_process

```odin
loop_recorder_process :: proc(user: rawptr, b: ^backend.Io_Block)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). (apart from the deliberate stall)

### loop_recorder_wait

```odin
loop_recorder_wait :: proc(r: ^Loop_Recorder, frames: i64, timeout: time.Duration) -> bool
```

Waits until the recorder has processed `frames` frames. False on timeout.

### analyze_loopback

```odin
analyze_loopback :: proc(play: []f32, rec: []f32, max_lag: int) -> (res: Loopback_Result)
```

Aligns `rec` to `play` and measures how exactly it is a scaled copy.
`play` must be a non-periodic signal (noise) for the alignment to be unique.

### device_lock

```odin
device_lock :: proc(name: string) -> Device_Lock
```

Blocks until this process and thread hold the lock for the shared device `name`
(a short identifier, used in a file or mutex name). Release with `device_unlock`.

### device_unlock

```odin
device_unlock :: proc(l: Device_Lock)
```

Releases a lock taken by `device_lock`.

### expect_near

```odin
expect_near :: proc(t: ^testing.T, actual: f64, expected: f64, tolerance: f64, what: string = "", loc: runtime.Source_Code_Location = #caller_location) -> bool
```

Fails the test if |actual - expected| > tolerance, printing both values, the
difference and `what`. Returns whether the check passed.

### expect_clean_render

```odin
expect_clean_render :: proc(t: ^testing.T, r: Render_Report, loc: runtime.Source_Code_Location = #caller_location) -> bool
```

The checks every render must pass: prepared OK, no rt allocations,
every output sample written and finite, no dropped output events.

### expect_block_invariant

```odin
expect_block_invariant :: proc(t: ^testing.T, factory: Node_Factory, input: Audio_Buffer, cfg: Render_Config, patterns: []Block_Pattern, tolerance: f64 = 1e-6, name: string = "block_invariance", loc: runtime.Source_Code_Location = #caller_location) -> bool
```

Renders the same input/events with every pattern in `patterns` (each through a
fresh node from `factory`) and requires all outputs to match the first within
`tolerance`. This is the main proof of sample-accurate, block-independent DSP.

### window_value

```odin
window_value :: proc(w: Window, i: int, n: int) -> f64
```

Coefficient of window `w` at sample `i` of an `n`-sample (symmetric) window. 1 when n <= 1.

### next_pow2

```odin
next_pow2 :: proc(n: int) -> int
```

Smallest power of two >= n (1 for n <= 1).

### fft

```odin
fft :: proc(data: []complex128, inverse: bool = false)
```

In-place iterative radix-2 FFT. len(data) must be a power of two.
The inverse is not normalized; divide by n yourself.

### spectrum

```odin
spectrum :: proc(x: []f32, sample_rate: f64, window: Window = Window.Hann, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> Spectrum
```

Windowed, zero-padded FFT of `x`. The magnitudes are allocated from `allocator`
(free with `spectrum_destroy`); FFT scratch comes from context.temp_allocator.

### spectrum_destroy

```odin
spectrum_destroy :: proc(s: ^Spectrum, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator)
```

Frees a spectrum's magnitudes with the allocator `spectrum` used, and zeroes it.

### spectrum_bin_hz

```odin
spectrum_bin_hz :: proc(s: Spectrum, k: int) -> f64
```

Center frequency in Hz of bin `k`.

### spectrum_peak

```odin
spectrum_peak :: proc(s: Spectrum) -> (bin: int, freq_hz: f64, magnitude: f64)
```

The bin with the largest magnitude, ignoring DC (bin 0), with its frequency in Hz
and linear amplitude.

### silence

```odin
silence :: proc(out: []f32)
```

Fills `out` with zeros.

### dc

```odin
dc :: proc(out: []f32, value: f32)
```

Fills `out` with the constant `value`.

### impulse

```odin
impulse :: proc(out: []f32, at: int = 0, amplitude: f32 = 1)
```

Zeros `out` and sets frame `at` to `amplitude`. An out-of-range `at` leaves pure silence.

### step

```odin
step :: proc(out: []f32, at: int = 0, amplitude: f32 = 1)
```

0 before frame `at`, `amplitude` from `at` on.

### sine

```odin
sine :: proc(out: []f32, sample_rate: f64, freq_hz: f64, amplitude: f64 = 1, phase: f64 = 0)
```

Sine of `freq_hz` and peak `amplitude` (linear), starting at `phase` radians at frame 0.

### log_sweep

```odin
log_sweep :: proc(out: []f32, sample_rate: f64, f0_hz: f64, f1_hz: f64, amplitude: f64 = 1)
```

Exponential (log) sine sweep, Farina 2000. Good for frequency response and distortion.

### rng_next_u64

```odin
rng_next_u64 :: proc(r: ^Rng) -> u64
```

Next 64 random bits; advances `r`.

### rng_next_f64

```odin
rng_next_f64 :: proc(r: ^Rng) -> f64
```

Uniform in [0, 1).

### rng_range

```odin
rng_range :: proc(r: ^Rng, lo: int, hi: int) -> int
```

Uniform integer in [lo, hi] inclusive (lo if hi <= lo). Has a tiny modulo bias,
fine for tests.

### white_noise

```odin
white_noise :: proc(out: []f32, seed: u64, amplitude: f64 = 1)
```

Uniform white noise in [-amplitude, amplitude).

### pink_noise

```odin
pink_noise :: proc(out: []f32, seed: u64, amplitude: f64 = 1)
```

Pink noise via Paul Kellet's refined filter on white noise. Roughly -3 dB/octave.

### artifacts_root

```odin
artifacts_root :: proc() -> string
```

Artifacts (actual/expected/diff WAVs + info) go here on failure.
Override with FIRE_ARTIFACTS_DIR. Render plots with: python3 scripts/plot.py <dir>

### update_golden_requested

```odin
update_golden_requested :: proc() -> bool
```

True when FIRE_UPDATE_GOLDEN is set to anything but "" or "0"; `expect_golden`
then rewrites golden files instead of comparing.

### artifact_dir

```odin
artifact_dir :: proc(name: string) -> string
```

Creates `<artifacts>/<name>/` and returns its path (temp-allocated).

### write_artifact

```odin
write_artifact :: proc(name: string, label: string, b: Audio_Buffer)
```

Writes `<artifacts>/<name>/<label>.wav`. Handy for dumping intermediate signals.

### write_artifact_note

```odin
write_artifact_note :: proc(name: string, text: string)
```

Writes `text` to `<artifacts>/<name>/info.txt`. Errors are ignored.

### expect_golden

```odin
expect_golden :: proc(t: ^testing.T, golden_dir: string, name: string, actual: Audio_Buffer, tolerance: f64 = 1e-5, loc: runtime.Source_Code_Location = #caller_location) -> bool
```

Compares `actual` against `<golden_dir>/<name>.wav` with an absolute
per-sample tolerance. With FIRE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1, the golden file is (re)written
and the test passes. A missing golden file fails unless updating.

### dump_comparison

```odin
dump_comparison :: proc(name: string, expected: Audio_Buffer, actual: Audio_Buffer, r: Compare_Result)
```

Writes expected/actual/diff WAVs and an info note for a failed comparison.

### block_sequence

```odin
block_sequence :: proc(sizes: ..int) -> Block_Sequence
```

Builds a `Block_Sequence` from 1 to 16 sizes (asserts otherwise). Sizes may be 0.

### default_render_config

```odin
default_render_config :: proc() -> Render_Config
```

48 kHz, 512-frame max block, stereo out, fixed full-size blocks, playing at
120 BPM, flush-to-zero on, room for 4096 output events per block.

### render_report_destroy

```odin
render_report_destroy :: proc(r: ^Render_Report)
```

Frees `events_out` and zeroes the report.

### render

```odin
render :: proc(node: ^core.Node, input: Audio_Buffer, cfg: Render_Config, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> (out: Audio_Buffer, report: Render_Report)
```

Renders `input.frames + cfg.tail_frames` frames through `node`. The output has
`cfg.out_channels` channels. The node is prepared here and released at the end;
the caller still owns (and destroys) it.

### standard_block_patterns

```odin
standard_block_patterns :: proc(max_block: int) -> [5]Block_Pattern
```

The block-size patterns every DSP test should survive.

### run_latency_probe

```odin
run_latency_probe :: proc(dev: ^backend.Device, timeout: time.Duration = 10 * time.Second) -> (frames: int, quality: f64, ok: bool)
```

Runs a `record.Latency_Probe` on an opened (not started) device, from
its first input channel to every output channel, and returns what it
measured. Starts and stops the device.

### probe_create

```odin
probe_create :: proc(capacity: int = 65536, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> (core.Node, ^Probe)
```

Creates a probe node and returns it along with its state. `capacity` is the number
of events and of blocks the log holds (allocated in prepare with the prepare
allocator). The node and state come from `allocator`; destroy with core.node_destroy.

### probe_events

```odin
probe_events :: proc(p: ^Probe) -> []Probe_Event
```

The events recorded so far, in arrival order. A view into the log, not a copy.

### probe_blocks

```odin
probe_blocks :: proc(p: ^Probe) -> []Probe_Block
```

The process calls recorded so far, in order. A view into the log, not a copy.

### probe_destroy

```odin
probe_destroy :: proc(n: ^core.Node, p: ^Probe)
```

Frees the probe's log and the probe itself (the same as core.node_destroy).

### stretch_case_freq_map

```odin
stretch_case_freq_map :: proc "contextless"(f: f32) -> f32
```

The custom frequency map case 1 uses (frequencies as fractions of the
sample rate): unchanged below 0.02, then spread out by 1.25.

### stretch_case_input

```odin
stretch_case_input :: proc(c: Stretch_Case, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> [][]f32
```

The input for a reference case: `c.channels` channels of `c.in_frames`
frames (channel 1 of a stereo case is the signal delayed by 7 ms at 70%).
Deterministic. Allocates with `allocator`.

### trap_allocator

```odin
trap_allocator :: proc(t: ^Trap_Allocator) -> mem.Allocator
```

An allocator backed by `t`: every request except feature queries and free(nil)
fails with .Out_Of_Memory and is counted in `t.violations`. Install it as
context.allocator around code that must not allocate (for example a device callback).

### wav_write

```odin
wav_write :: proc(path: string, b: Audio_Buffer) -> Wav_Error
```

Writes 32-bit IEEE float WAV.

### wav_read

```odin
wav_read :: proc(path: string, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> (b: Audio_Buffer, err: Wav_Error)
```

Reads PCM 16/24/32-bit int and 32/64-bit float WAV (including WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE).

## Variables

### stretch_reference_cases

```odin
stretch_reference_cases: [26]Stretch_Case
```

The reference cases. Ratios above 2 (and below 0.5) make Signalsmith
Stretch randomise phases with the C++ standard library's generator, so
those recordings are only reproducible with the same library (they were
made with macOS's libc++).
